request.spec:
A sheet's children are the sheets naming it as their parent. The screen gains consolidated figures
over the sheet and all its descendants: the number of people, the due-total (each sheet's due-total
as that sheet shows it, added up) and the overdue-total (likewise). A sheet with no children shows
its own figures there.

agent.result_text:
The screen now shows consolidated figures — people, due-total and overdue-total — across the sheet and every sheet below it, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:**
- **Server:** a new read-only endpoint, `POST /api/rollup/descendants/list` in `rollup/RollupController.java`, goes through the sheet's children, their children and so on. It works out each one's figures with the existing `RollupService.snapshot`, so every sub-sheet's due- and overdue-total is calculated as that sheet would show it, using its own today, rates and settings. It then adds them up. It never visits the same sheet twice, so a bad parent link can't send it round in a loop. To find a sheet's children I added `findByParentIdOrderByIdAsc` to `SheetRepository`. No database change was needed, because the `parent_id` column already exists.
- **Screen:** the header (`header/header.ts`) has a second row of figures under the test IDs `consolidated-people-count`, `consolidated-due-total` and `consolidated-overdue-total`. The people component fetches the sub-sheets' figures each time a sheet loads and adds them to the sheet's own figures. A sheet with no children therefore shows exactly its own figures.

**Behaviours to know about:**
- **Sub-sheet figures don't update live.** The sheet's own share changes straight away after an edit, but the sub-sheets' figures are only re-read when the sheet is loaded again. That fits the app's "re-load to see other changes" model.
- **The people count includes retired people,** the same as the existing header count.
- **"As of" view not tested:** the endpoint path ends in `/list` so that this view will answer it. No test covers consolidated figures in that view, so I haven't checked them there.
